parties:
Chairman, Bangladesh Water Development Board and others ------ Petitioner
Vs. 
Chairman, Divisional Labour Court, Rajshahi and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Nurul Islam J: This Rule was issued at instance of the petitioner calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 22-10-1990 passed by the learned Chairman, Labour Court Rajshahi in LRO Case No. 24 of 1990 (Annexure B) should not be set aside. 

 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the respondent No. 2, Md Abdur Razzaque filed an application under section 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969 in the Labour Court, Rajshahi on 10-3-1990 stating, inter alia, that he was appointed as pump operator in Division III of Pirgonj, Thakurgaon on 23-11-1966 and then he was transferred to Baliadangi Branch as light pump driver in 1973 in pursuance of the office Memo No. 134/1/100 dated 23-5-1974. The respondent No. 2 discharged the work of ''patwari'' of some deep tubewells and then he was transferred to Baliadangi Water Development Subdivision on 6-2-1978 to hold the charge of patwari and since then he has been working as such. The respondent No. 2 is getting less salary from patwari although he has been doing the duty of patwari. The respondent No. 2 made representations to the authorities on several occasions but got no relief and lastly, he made representation on 29-11-1989 stating that he is entitled to get an amount of Taka 38,068.81 as his salary from 23-5-1974 to February, 1990. Getting no reply of his representation he filed IRO Case No. 24 of 1990 under section 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969 for getting scale of pay of patwari from 23-5-74. The petitioners as respondents appeared and took several adjournments for filing written statements. Subsequently the petitioner did not contest the case and the case was decreed ex parte on 22-10-1990 and the Labour Court directed the petitioner to give scale of pay of patwari from 23-5-1974 within 30 days from the date of the order (Annexure B). The petitioner filed an application under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the aforesaid order and the said application is numbered as Misc. Case No. 3 of 1990. The said Misc. Case was rejected on 25-1-1990. Being dissatisfied with the aforesaid order of ex parte decree dated 22-10-1990 the petitioner preferred this application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr. Abdul Halim Chaklader, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that the respondent No.2 was appointed as ''pump operator'' and while he was working as such he was given charge of ''patwari'' in addition to his work as pump driver and the post of patwari is superior post with higher scale of pay. He further submitted that the petitioner was never promoted to the post of patwari or to officiate in the post of patwari on promotion and, as such, he is not entitled to scale of pay of patwari. The learned Chairman of Labour Court without considering this aspect of the case directed the petitioner to give respondent No. 2 the scale of pay of patwari from 23-5-1974. He again submitted that an employee cannot claim the scale of pay of superior post unless he is promoted or appointed to such post. In the petition before the Labour Court ie Annexure-A it is found that the respondent No. 2 prayed for pay and scale of patwari from 23-5-74 that is, the date of his work as patwari. The Annexure-1 of the Counter-affidavit, filed by respondent No. 2 shows that by memo No. 1314/1/100 dated 23-5-1974 communicated to respondent No. 2 vide Memo No. 151 (3) dated 26-9-74 he was directed to take charge of patwari of some deep tube-wells when he has been working in his substantive post as pump driver. But by the aforesaid Annexure-1, the respondent No. 2 was not promoted to the post of patwari and he was simply given the charge of patwari of that station. The respondent No. 2 filed the petition before the authority of Water Development Board on 26-7-89 and this petition is made as Annexure H to the original petition. In annexure-H the respondent No. 2 admitted that he received the charge of patwari on 28-5-1974 as per direction of memo dated 23-5-74 and since then he has been working as such and that he prayed for promotion to the post of patwari and for this he has given several petitions to the authorities but he was not promoted to the post of patwari till today ie on 26-8-89 and he also prayed for charge allowance of patwari from 28-5-74. The Annexure-H clearly shows that the petitioner was neither promoted to the post of patwari nor he has been officiating as patwari and that he did not pray for the scale of pay of patwari to the authority in this petition and, on the contrary, he prayed for charge allowance to which he is legally entitled. 

 5. Mr. Marfat Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2, submitted that the petitioner was given charge of patwari and he has been officiating in the post of patwari since 1974 and he is entitled to the scale of pay of patwari as he has been working in charge of patwari for a long time. We have already said that the post of patwari is a superior post and the petitioner himself admitted in his petition Annexure H that he has not been promoted to the post of patwari though he made prayer for promotion to the post of patwari to the relevant authorities. The respondent No. 2 was appointed as pump driver and while he had been working as pump driver he was given charge of patwari in addition to his own duty without promoting him as patwari. An employee cannot get scale of pay of superior post unless and until he is promoted and appointed to that post. An employee of junior post can hold charge of superior post in addition to his own duty and for this he is entitled to charge allowance if there is any such provision in the service rule. In the instant case the petitioner was not promoted to the post of patwari and, as such, he is not entitled to scale of pay of patwari which is superior post to pump driver. The learned Advocate for the respondent No.2 relied on a decision reported in 23 DLR (SC) 49 (The Postmaster General Eastern Circle, (EP) Dacca and another vs. Muhammad Hashim). Their Lordships held 

 6. The facts and circumstance of the aforesaid case is not identical with the present case. In the instant case the respondent was not promoted to officiate to the post of patwari and he discharged the duties of patwari holding his substantive post as pump driver. So, this observation is of no help to the present case. The Labour Court by the impugned ex parte order allowed the prayer of respondent No. 2 without considering the facts and circumstances of the case in the manner we discussed above. So, the impugned order passed by the Labour Court is not legal. So, we find that the respondent No. 2 has been working as patwari in charge and for this he prayed for charge allowance (Annexure H). Rule 33(d) of Bangladesh Water Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 reads as follows: 

 7. According to the above Rules an employee holding additional charge of another post he shall be entitled to pay of his post plus additional 20% pay as charge allowance subject to maximum of Taka 200.00. In the instant case the respondent No. 2 is entitled to 20% of pay to the maximum of Taka 200.00 as charge allowance for holding the charge of patwari since 26-5-74 ie the date of taking over the charge of patwari.
